collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE X: GROWING UP, GROWING OLD AND EVERYDAY JOY (LCJ-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
The rest of the owner's 100 Living Culture ideas and the world-inspired 50: secret languages and forgotten words, coming of age, elders who will not retire, healers' oaths, failed discoveries, masks and clothes and masterpieces nobody wanted, talent shows, ridiculous hats and the day nobody worked.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager who does not speak has a story for the gathering: let them tell it their way, or have a friend speak it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) does not speak with words, and never has. (subject.He/she) communicates with signs, drawings and the expressions on (subject.his/her) face. (subject.He/she) has a story to tell the gathering: how (subject.he/she) found the lost child in the swamp last week. (friend) has offered to speak it for (subject.him/her). What should happen?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) tells it with signs, drawings in the sand and a very dramatic pantomime of the swamp. The gathering is silent and riveted. When (subject.he/she) acts out finding the child, the whole village cheers. Nobody needed a single word.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) speaks the story while (subject) signs it. It works well, but (friend) gets a few details wrong, and (subject) corrects (friend.him/her) by pointing, firmly. The gathering laughs. Next time, (subject) tells it alone.
